President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he’s going to explain why each candidate won and lost in the midterm elections, but CNN’s John King said there’s really just one reason.

And that’s Trump himself.

The Republican Party got trounced on Tuesday, and Trump’s handpicked candidates, in particular, lost lopsided races, often in deep red territory.

But writing on Truth Social, Trump wouldn’t take any blame. He insisted that if he had been on the ballot, Republicans would have won. Then, the president said he would become “a political pundit” to explain the results.

“Let me help you, sir, as you start your new career,” King said, then broke out the map.

“The president went here and said, ‘Vote like I’m on the ballot,’” King said, circling Ohio. He circled South Carolina and added, “He went here and said, ‘Vote like I’m on the ballot.’”

Ditto for Texas: “He went here several times and said, ‘Vote like I’m on the ballot.’”

King continued to circle the states Trump had visited and made that same plea that his supporters vote like he’s on the ballot ― and in nearly every case, his candidates lost.

“He went to states he won by double digits and said, ‘Vote like I’m on the ballot,’” King said. “Well, they did. They did in Trump country, in rural America, in places where he had won convincingly. People said ‘Enough.’”

He went on to say voters have had enough of high fuel prices caused by a war that Trump had promised not to start ― and that was just one of a number of issues that has voters fed up.
